in_text_mentions: No complications occurred, in particular no excessive bleeding, neither during the surgery nor in the week after. Mandibular sensitivity returned with the pass of the dental anesthesia. Seven days after surgery, the sutures were removed. Initial histologic examination revealed a dentigerous cyst (Figure 3). One year after surgery, a new panoramic radiograph was performed, revealing the complete healing of the site (Figure 2).

Bleeding is more likely to result from repetitive pressure or trauma on the overlying oral mucosa from the denture and is least likely to be from the cyst. The differential diagnosis considered a hemorrhagic eruptive cyst, but we considered this theory unlikely due to the age of the patient. The histological examination reported in Figure 3 confirmed the nature of the dentigerous cyst.

panels.figure_caption: Histopathological examination of the cyst Magnification: 40x
in_text_mentions: Histopathological investigation revealed a cystic cavity lined by two- to three-layer thick epithelium with characteristics similar to reduced enamel epithelium. The epithelium connective tissue interface was flat. The underlying connective tissue capsule was fibrous with mild chronic inflammatory cells infiltrated. A few areas of extravasculated red blood cells (RBCs) were also appreciable along with peripheral areas exhibiting reactive bone formation. The histopathologic examination confirmed the diagnosis of a dentigerous cyst (Figure 3).

panels.rationale: CBCT of the mandible shows a well-defined unilocular radiolucency around the crown of horizontally impacted tooth 48, consistent with a classic dentigerous cyst. Caption and in-text support dentigerous cyst; annotations mark the inferior alveolar nerve canal.

in_text_mentions: ding anterior-posteriorly from the cementoenamel junction (CEJ) of tooth 48 to the distal aspect of tooth 47 and superior-inferiorly from the crestal bone to approximately 8.8 mm from the inferior border of the mandible. Apically displaced right inferior alveolar nerve canal (IANC) was noted. Thinning/Discontinuity of both buccal and lingual cortical plate with respect to tooth 48 was seen. No signs of root resorption or fracture were noted with respect to tooth 47. Infra-erupted tooth 47 and approximation of right IANC with both mesial and distal roots of tooth 47 was also seen (Figures 2-3).

panels.rationale: Single H&E histopathology panel of a human mandibular surgical specimen from a patient with an infected complex odontoma associated with a dentigerous cyst. The caption and in-text mentions describe the fibrous cyst wall lined focally by non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, which is the defining histologic feature of a dentigerous cyst; the odontomatous tissue and chronic osteitis are co-existing/complicating elements (recorded as proposed findings, as they are not in the allowed vocabulary). No skin, mucosa or clinical surface is shown, so skin tone and ethnicity are not assessable and no demographic data are given.

The middle portion shows the dense fibrous connective tissue forming the cyst wall. The lower portion demonstrates irregular necrotic bony trabeculae consistent with chronic osteitis.

panels.rationale: Single-panel panoramic radiograph of a real patient from a case report titled 'Mandibular Fracture Associated with a Dentigerous Cyst'. The in-text description specifies a well-defined mandibular radiolucency spanning the first premolar to second molar region with displacement of the lower left second premolar toward the inferior border and an associated pathological fracture, matching dentigerous cyst radiographic findings (well-corticated radiolucency, unerupted/displaced tooth crown, cortical expansion/bone destruction). No ethnicity or age stated in caption or text; skin tone not assessable on a radiograph. The 'L' laterality marker is an annotation.

in_text_mentions: hically, a well-defined radiolucency was identified in the body of the mandible on the left side. The radiolucency extended from the first premolar region to the second molar area. It seemed to have destroyed bone almost from the edentulous alveolar crest to the inferior border of the mandible. A small ill-defined area was observed in the anterior border of the lesion. The lesion was associated with an obvious bony fracture in the inferior border of the mandible. The relatively large size of the lesion had pushed the lower left second premolar to the inferior border of the mandible (Figure 1).

plate_findings.evidence: lined by a non-keratinized thin stratified epithelium (H&E 20x)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A is a real patient histology image showing the classic dentigerous cyst lining: a non-keratinized thin stratified squamous epithelium with a fibrous connective tissue wall. The article and in-text histopathological diagnosis identify dentigerous cyst. B: Panel B is a real patient histology image from the dentigerous cyst case showing basophilic ovoid calcifications in the connective wall and odontogenic epithelial cords. Calcifications are a less common variant feature of this dentigerous cyst. C: Panel C is a real patient histology image from the dentigerous cyst case showing ovoid calcifications with peripheral eosinophilic areas and irregular disposition. These calcifications represent the variant dentigerous cyst with capsular/intracystic calcifications described in the article.
panels.attribution_text: Borrás-Ferreres et al. Dentigerous cyst with parietal and intracystic calcifications: A case report and literature review.. Journal of clinical and experimental dentistry 2018. doi:10.4317/jced.54505. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: A) Cystic lesion with a fibrous connective wall without signs of inflammation and lined by a non-keratinized thin stratified epithelium (H&E 20x). B) Basophilic ovoid calcifications present at the connective wall and odontogenic epithelial cords (H&E 20x). C) Ovoid calcifications and peripheral eosinophilic areas with irregular disposition (H&E 40x).
in_text_mentions: Microscopically, a cystic wall constituted by fibrous connective tissue was observed. Interestingly, some basophilic globular calcified ovoid deposits were seen into its thickness. Furthermore, some of these had a greater size and presented a cemento-osseous structure with apposition lines and included cells. Some capsular deposits showed a non-keratinized stratified thin epithelial lining, focally detached (Fig. 2). The histopathological diagnosis was dentigerous cyst with capsular calcifications.

panels.rationale: Single reconstructed panoramic CBCT image of a real patient showing the classic pericoronal radiolucency surrounding the crown of an impacted mandibular right third molar, matching the dentigerous cyst finding vocabulary. Caveat lowering confidence: the article title states the lesion proved to be a glandular odontogenic cyst mimicking a dentigerous cyst, so the panel documents a dentigerous-cyst-like radiographic presentation rather than a histologically confirmed dentigerous cyst; attribution rests on the captioned pericoronal/impacted-crown appearance. Red annotation line marks the mandibular canal and a scale/reference text is overlaid (annotations present). No patient age or ethnicity is given; skin tone not assessable on a radiograph.

The imaging showed a horizontally impacted mandibular right third molar (48) and a mesioangularly impacted mandibular left third molar (38). A well-defined ovoid hypodense lesion was noted surrounding the crown of tooth 48, suggestive of a cystic lesion. The lesion measured approximately 13.8 × 15.4 × 9.7 mm and extended to the distal root of tooth 47, with associated bone loss. The mesial aspect of the crown of 48 was in close contact with the distal surface of 47. No root resorption or caries was observed in relation to 47 (Figure 1).
